name: How much contingency should I add to an office remodel budget?

mainEntity.name: What percentage contingency is smart for an office renovation in Los Angeles, especially in older buildings?
mainEntity.text: What percentage contingency is smart for an office renovation in Los Angeles, especially in older buildings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Contingency is one of the most important parts of an office renovation budget because commercial projects often uncover surprises after demolition starts. In older Los Angeles buildings, hidden plumbing, outdated electrical, structural issues, asbestos, or accessibility corrections can all increase costs. A smaller cosmetic refresh may only need a modest contingency, but a full tenant improvement or renovation in an older shell usually deserves more room. The exact percentage depends on how much of the existing building will be opened up and how complete the design documents are before bidding. To avoid budget stress, separate contingency from allowances and make sure the contractor explains what conditions would trigger its use.
acceptedAnswer.description: A common contingency range for office renovations is 10% to 20%, with older buildings and more complex scopes needing the higher end. Contingency helps cover hidden conditions, permit revisions, material changes, and unexpected utility or code issues.
